Scope 003 review verdict: Approve with nits; no blocker, no major, 15 minor and 18 nits; the test reviewer and the document reviewer each rated one finding major (t1, d1) and the main reviewer rates both minor after checking code and spec
nodes.rationale: t1 is minor because an open answer would still need the first cluster entry, the journal and fresh evidence to agree; d1 is minor because the decision behind row k is written down, reasoned (decision 17) and judged right, and only one sentence in the PRD is missing.

nodes.label: Scope 003 review summary: the change adds the control, cluster, node and identity keys, identifier and generation types and the crate pool-control; no Open unless configuration, journal and a fresh sample agree; the open limits are for scope 004 (read m1 to m3 first)
nodes.rationale: What is left are limits of the design that the next slice has to close, not defects of this one; the most important is that a Ready state is a copy of the journal from the moment of the start (m1).

nodes.label: How the scope 003 review was run (six steps): full read of the production files, three parallel reviewers, a built pool binary with made inputs, a temporary pool-control test, five mutation probes and cargo test --workspace --locked

Scope 003 review step: every production file in the range read in full (five files of crates/pool-control/src, four of crates/pool-config/src, apps/pool/src/report.rs, manifests, lockfile, workspace.rs, three baseline files, prove-checks.sh); spec 0003 read first

Scope 003 review step: three reviewers ran in parallel without seeing each other's results (claude-sonnet-5-5 production code, claude-fable-5-2 tests, claude-opus-5-5 documents); the main reviewer checked each finding against the code before it entered the file

Scope 003 review probe: pool built at be06393 and pool check-config run on made inputs (CRLF, tabs, no final line feed, a byte order mark, an empty file, a canary in keys, table names, wrong typed values and array entries); no leak in twelve canary runs
Scope 003 review probe: a temporary test against pool-control with two clusters, edge times and a journal that changed after the start; its file was removed and the tree was clean afterwards

Scope 003 review mutation probes: the code was changed on purpose five times and put back; the changes that every test survived are named in t1 (cluster duplicate id call removed), t2 (three skip rules) and t3 (E0451 changed to E0308)
nodes.rationale: A mutation probe: if the tests still pass after a deliberate change, nothing pins that line.

nodes.label: Scope 003 review test run: cargo test --workspace --locked gave 238 passed, 0 failed (78 in apps/pool, 3 in its unit tests, 25 and 95 in pool-config, 3 and 26 in pool-control, 8 documentation tests)

The five questions of the scope 003 review brief: Open without full agreement, file text leak and LineIndex, the public contract of spec 0001, soundness of the guards, and whether spec 0003 matches the code

Scope 003 review question 1: nothing gets Open without full agreement from honest inputs; writer_admission returns Open only at admission.rs:305 and Authority is made only at authority.rs:183; three caller limits remain (m1, m2, m3)
nodes.rationale: An age equal to the expiry is closed and one nanosecond less is open.There is no arithmetic that can overflow: the age is a checked_sub and the generations only compare. Probes: an expiry of zero is closed, a now before the sample is closed, a conflict in cluster b closes b and leaves a open, a cluster only the journal knows is authority.cluster_unknown.

nodes.label: Scope 003 review question 2: no file text leak found (hand written Debug prints [REDACTED], a Finding holds a code, a constant key and two numbers) and LineIndex gave the right line and column at every edge, with no quadratic path; see m5 and m8

Scope 003 review question 3: the public contract of spec 0001 is unchanged; apps/pool/src/report.rs changed by one line (the Location::KeyAt arm, :106); OUTPUT_VERSION, SUPPORTED_CONFIG_VERSION, the valid report, the seven old codes and the exit status are as before

Scope 003 review question 4: the guards are sound; the baseline changes are exactly the three lines spec 0003 names and the new W4 lockfile check works for an entry at the start, middle and end of the file, with one known way around it that a test pins as intended (m4)

Scope 003 review question 5: spec 0003 matches the code closely (reason names and order, refusals, finding codes, key paths, constants); the dated notes in spec 0001 and spec 0002 add text and rewrite no sentence, but two say a little more than is true (m4, n13)
nodes.rationale: The notes change what a reader has to take as current (0001 AC-1, AC-12 and AC-13 describe the first build only, the first secret reference key arrives one scope earlier, three baseline files differ, W4 has one more check, case 17 edits another file); each note says so plainly and names 0003 AC-13 as the current statement, which the reviewer calls an honest way to do it.

nodes.label: Scope 003 review Minor m1 (admission.rs:182, authority.rs:137): a Ready state cannot learn of a conflict latch set after the start, so writes reopen once the second primary drops out of sight; fix: a spec 0003 decision before scope 004 plus a walk from row d to row o
nodes.rationale: Suggested fix: decide it in spec 0003 before scope 004 dispatches SQL (a new item of Follow-up 4 or a criterion next to AC-16): either a pool-control function that takes a Ready state and a Closed that asks for the latch and returns the state with the latch set, or a rule that the daemon reads and classifies the journal again after every write, plus the memory for a failed write; then add a walk from row d to row o through the real functions, with the second primary gone in the second call.This is the case R-19 and PRD-006 AC-2 are about: the other primary is still there, it just cannot be seen any more, and writes open again. It is the same kind of gap as the one 0003 AC-16 closed, where the function trusted its caller. Nothing calls the function yet, so nothing is wrong today; it will be wrong on the first day of scope 004 unless that slice adds the missing piece inside pool-control. The same holds for the authority revision in an Open answer. Owner: the architect for the spec, then the developer.

nodes.label: Scope 003 review Minor m2 (authority.rs:18, :35): StoreProbe, StoredAuthority, ApprovedTopology and Quarantine have public fields, so any crate can build a journal value and 0003 AC-12 holds only by convention; fix: private fields or a W3/W5 line in scope 004
nodes.rationale: Suggested fix: when scope 004 puts the journal reader inside pool-control, make the fields private and give the tests one constructor that runs the same checks as the reader, or add a line to rule W3 or W5 that keeps StoreProbe::Present out of every other crate; record the choice in Follow-up 4.AC-12 shows that Authority, EligiblePrimary, Closed and BootstrapPlan cannot be built outside the crate, but with a free StoreProbe that proof does not carry far: the one thing that turns into authority is the thing anyone can make. Today only tests do. The spec names the condition (the journal reader stays the only code that builds a StoreProbe) and no check enforces it. Owner: the architect.

nodes.label: Scope 003 review Minor m3 (observation.rs:140): a latest sample dated after now, or two samples tied at the latest time, count as no evidence, which hides a seen second primary on a node other than the writer; fix: a spec decision for scope 004 on the caller's duty
nodes.rationale: Suggested fix: the smallest is a duty of the caller, written into the documentation comment of writer_admission and into Follow-up 4 (read now after the list of observations is fixed, pass at most one sample per node); a stricter one is in the rule itself: for a node other than the writer, a latest sample that cannot be used closes with a reason of its own.Both inputs can happen in scope 004 without anyone doing something strange: a probe result that lands a moment after the daemon read now is in the future of now, and two probe paths handing in the same sample tie. In both cases one admission can open while a second primary is in the list. Owner: the architect.

nodes.label: Scope 003 review Minor t1 (topology.rs:688): no test fails when the config.duplicate_id check for cluster.id is removed from cross_check (all 238 tests still pass; the code is right); fix: a test with two [[cluster]] entries of one id and one pinning the order of step 6.1
nodes.rationale: Suggested fix: one test with two [[cluster]] entries of the same id, and one with a repeated cluster, node and identity id in one file to pin the order clusters, nodes, identities of step 6.1.writer_admission and plan_bootstrap take the first cluster with a given id, so a repeated id would carry a second expected_writer and system identifier that nothing reads. The test reviewer rated this major; the main reviewer rates it minor because an open answer would still need the first entry, the journal and fresh evidence to agree, so losing the check would confuse an operator and not open a write. It is the first test the reviewer would add. Owner: the tester.

nodes.label: Scope 003 review Minor t2 (topology.rs:728, :731, :772): three skip rules of the cross checks are pinned by no test (a bad cluster id, a node with a bad cluster, the endpoint check on a node whose port failed); fix: three small cases in tests/validate.rs
nodes.rationale: The three changes every test survived: skipping the expected_writer check for all clusters when one cluster has a bad id, running that check although a node has a bad cluster, and letting the endpoint check read a node whose port failed (AC-15 made input 3). Suggested fix: two clusters where one has a bad id and the other a wrong writer; a writer whose node has a bad cluster; two nodes with the same host and port = 0.These are the rules that make one mistake give one finding (AC-2). They were reworded after the verification of milestone 2, so they are the part of the validation order most likely to be touched again. Owner: the tester.

nodes.label: Scope 003 review Minor m4 (tools/repo-check/src/workspace.rs:236): the W4 lockfile check is passed by a [[patch.unused]] table after the last local package, the test at :1210 pins that and prove-checks.sh has no case for it; fix: end an entry at any line starting with [
nodes.rationale: Suggested fix: end an entry at any line that starts with [ (a lockfile entry never holds a table of its own), change the sentence in spec 0003 and the pinned test with it, add one prove-checks.sh case that adds a local package to the lockfile and expects W4, and soften 'closes finding m14' in the spec 0002 note until then.The check exists for one case, a package Cargo treats as a member without being listed; that case still needs a change to the W1 baseline, which a reviewer sees, so the risk is small. But a guard with a known way around it and a test that calls the way around correct will be trusted more than it should be. Owner: the architect for the two sentences, the developer for the rest.

nodes.label: Scope 003 review Minor m5 (topology.rs:399, report.rs:139): one file at the size limit (349514 empty identity entries) gives 2097084 findings, up to 251 MB of output and 539 MB of memory; fix: a BufWriter in check_config, then a spec decision on a findings limit
nodes.rationale: Measured with the debug build on a file of 1048574 bytes: the human format wrote 190709698 bytes in 2.5 seconds with a peak of 405 MB, the JSON format 251525214 bytes in 8.5 seconds with a peak of 539 MB; the time is linear and each human finding is one system call through the line buffered stdout lock (main.rs:77). Suggested fix: wrap the locked stdout in a BufWriter in check_config, then decide in the spec whether the number of findings gets a limit (one config.missing_key per entry with no key at all, or a fixed top count with a last line).The file belongs to the operator, so this is not an attack, but it is the same function the daemon will call at a start and at a reload, and bounded resources then means about 500 times the input. AC-15 bounds the time for the made inputs and says nothing about the number of findings. A limit changes AC-3, so it is the architect's call. Owner: the developer for the buffer, the architect for the limit.

nodes.label: Scope 003 review Minor t3 (admission.rs:89, pool-config lib.rs:44): the compile_fail,E0451 documentation tests do not check the error code on Rust 1.100.0 (E0308 also passed) although verify.md:206 says so; fix: correct verify.md and pair each with a passing test
nodes.rationale: The four pool-control tests are at admission.rs:89, :137, authority.rs:128 and bootstrap.rs:57; the older ValidatedConfig test (lib.rs:44) names three of what are now eight fields, so it fails for the missing fields and would keep failing if the fields became public. Suggested fix: correct the sentence in verify.md, use the update form ValidatedConfig { config_version: 2, ..valid } whose only possible error is the private field, and add a passing documentation test beside each compile_fail test that uses the same paths through the public functions.These tests are the proof of the second half of AC-12 and of the AC-3 rule that validate is the only way to a ValidatedConfig. Each still catches the real mistake as long as its snippet has no other error; a renamed field or type turns it into a test that passes for the wrong reason, without a sign. Owner: the tester, and the checker for the sentence.

nodes.label: Scope 003 review Minor d1 (spec 0003 index.md:780, :855): row k of walk 3 keeps writes open when the second primary is a quarantined node, against the letter of PRD-006 AC-2, and the PRD does not say so; fix: add the exception or a dated note to PRD-006 AC-2
nodes.rationale: Suggested fix: add the exception to PRD-006 AC-2, or a dated note under it that points to spec 0003, and say in the spec that rule 10 leaves quarantined nodes out on purpose, so that scope 010 knows the exception also covers a quarantined node on a later timeline.The document reviewer rated this major; the main reviewer rates it minor. The decision is written down and reasoned (decision 17, heavy) and judged right: the quarantine is the reviewed answer to exactly that node, closing would let one returned old primary stop a cluster after a correct promotion, and POOL sends nothing to the quarantined node either way. What is missing is one sentence where the requirement lives. docs/prd/ is not a file a sub session may change, so this is for the lead. Owner: the lead and the architect.

nodes.label: Scope 003 review Minor m6 (admission.rs:238, :288, observation.rs:143): the cost of one writer admission grows with nodes times observations while the configuration allows about 13000 nodes; fix in scope 004: answer from the snapshot or index observations by node
nodes.rationale: Each call walks every node of the file, builds two lists and walks every observation for every node of the cluster; the member check at admission.rs:257 is members times nodes. Suggested fix: when scope 004 wires it, answer admission from the topology snapshot and call the function only when the configuration, the journal or an observation changes, or index the observations by node once; say which in the spec of scope 004.With three nodes it is nothing, but spec 0003 has scope 004 call the function at every session admission and again after the backend is acquired, the root guide asks for bounded work on the data path, and the validation time rule of the spec covers validate only. Owner: the architect of scope 004.

nodes.label: Scope 003 review Minor m7 (Cargo.toml:14): the workspace dependency pool-control is declared and taken by no member, so Cargo 1.100.0 warns on every command, against the AGENTS.md:31 rule; fix: take the line out until scope 004 adds the first use, or add a dated note
nodes.rationale: The warning is 'unused workspace dependency pool-control'; spec 0003 asks for the line now and no note in spec 0001 or AGENTS.md records the exception. Suggested fix: take the line out and let scope 004 add it in the commit that adds the first use (one sentence less in spec 0003), or keep it and add a dated note where the rule lives.The warning fails no check, so it will sit in the output of every check until scope 004, and a warning that is always there teaches people to stop reading warnings. A spec that orders what the root guide forbids leaves the next agent to guess which one wins. Rule W5 reads the manifests of the members and does not need the line. Owner: the architect to choose, the developer to apply.

nodes.label: Scope 003 review Minor m8 (topology.rs:456): names accept the control characters U+0080 to U+009F and direction characters such as U+202E, pinned by the test at topology.rs:894; fix: a spec decision before a name reaches any output (refuse them, or escape on output)
nodes.rationale: Suggested fix: either refuse the whole Unicode control class and the direction characters, or say in one sentence that the list is complete on purpose and that every later output escapes names.Nothing prints a name today and the telemetry table keeps names out of default output, but scope 004 sends the backend login and database to PostgreSQL and scope 009 will show identity routes to an administrator. U+009B is an escape lead on some terminals, and a direction override makes two entries look alike on a screen. Owner: the architect.

nodes.label: Scope 003 review Minor t4 (validate.rs:1446, check_config.rs:2284): the 0003 AC-4 canary tests put the secret text in string values only, not in an unknown key, a table name, an array entry or a wrong typed value; fix: one table driven test in each of the two files
nodes.rationale: The code is fine today, but those positions go through the parser error path, which holds the text of the key, and only a test keeps a later change from printing it. Owner: the tester.

nodes.label: Scope 003 review Minor t5 (pool-config lib.rs:579): LineIndex has no test of its own and nothing compares it with line_column (lib.rs:556); fix: one unit test that walks every offset of a few short texts and compares the two
nodes.rationale: Suggested fix: the texts should have CRLF, a tab, two, three and four byte characters and a length that is a multiple of 256, and the test compares LineIndex::line_column with line_column.The reviewer's probes gave the right positions, but the two functions have to agree for every offset, or a syntax finding and a value finding in the same file would count columns in two ways. Not covered through validate: a stride boundary inside a multi byte character, an offset at or past the end, a tab. Owner: the tester.

nodes.label: Scope 003 review Minor t6 (tools/repo-check/baseline/forbidden-source-patterns.txt): nothing automatic keeps a clock or a file read out of pool-control; the second half of 0003 AC-11 is a grep run by hand; fix: make the grep a guard (a change to rule W3) in scope 004
nodes.rationale: Adding Instant::now() to crates/pool-control/src/ would fail no test and no guard today. Suggested fix: when scope 004 decides where the journal reader lives, make the grep a guard, for example a list of patterns for the rule modules only; that is a change to rule W3 and needs a sentence in the spec.That pool-control reads no clock and no file is what makes the four walks run as tests and what scope 004 builds on. Scope 004 puts the journal reader into this crate, which is exactly when a file read or a clock read is most likely to slip into the rule functions. Owner: the architect of scope 004.

nodes.label: Strengths named by the scope 003 review (six): a small readable admission rule, closed as the default, an independent small domain test, no file text in findings by construction, a linear position lookup and a one line change to spec 0001 behaviour
Scope 003 review strength: the rule that matters most is small and readable; admit_ready is ninety lines, follows the order of the spec table one check at a time and has one place that returns Open

Scope 003 review strength: closed is the default everywhere (an inconsistent journal, an absent or different witness, a hold, an unknown cluster, a tie, a sample from the future for the writer, an age equal to the expiry)

Scope 003 review strength: the small domain test computes its answer with a rule of its own, in another shape than the code, and pins the count of open answers at 130 of 8192, so a change that opens one more case fails it
Scope 003 review strength: no text from the configuration file can reach a finding by construction, not by care, because the types that carry findings have no field that could hold it
Scope 003 review strength: the position lookup (LineIndex) is linear to build and a binary search to use, and it gave the right answer for every odd input the reviewer tried
Scope 003 review strength: the change to spec 0001 behaviour is one line of code and the old fixtures keep their results

Test coverage in the scope 003 review: test signal configured (the built in cargo test harness, no test dependency); every criterion a test can prove has a real test and the old spec 0001 tests were not weakened

Scope 003 review table of criteria 0003 AC-1 to AC-16 with proving tests and verdicts: all Real except AC-14 (checked by reading); gaps t1 and t2 on AC-2, t3 on AC-3 and AC-6, t4 on AC-4, m1 on AC-9, t6 on AC-11, m4 on AC-13; AC-15 is one wall clock sample

What no test covers in the scope 003 review, in the order to add it: the walk from row d to row o (m1), a repeated cluster id (t1), the three skip rules (t2), a lockfile proof case (m4), the canary in keys and names (t4), LineIndex against line_column (t5)
Not run in the scope 003 review: scripts/check.sh all, scripts/prove-checks.sh, the Linux build and the fuzz target; the lead ran the first two on main, and a run on macOS is not Linux evidence

Not run in the scope 003 review: CI on GitHub, which the verification record marks NOT_RUN with the user as owner; the Linux evidence in the record is a Docker container on the local machine and is labelled as that
Scope 003 review limit: the test reviewer and the document reviewer ran no cargo command; every claim that a changed line survived the tests was run by the main reviewer
